correctness.rationale: The valuation of j+1 counts the trailing base-b digits equal to b−1, even when b is composite. This proves Delta_j=1−(b−1)nu_b(j+1) modulo m; in any two consecutive increments at least one is +1. For any triple with a reverse occurrence, the two increments therefore include both +1 and −1, distinct for m≥3, so the endpoints agree. Applying this to all internal triples of a reversible word forces period two. An even-length nonpalindromic such word has, in one of its two orientations, the consecutive increments (−1,+1,−1); impossible because any −1 transition has endpoint divisible by b if b≥3 and by 4 if b=2. Thus every class at n≥3 is singleton, not necessarily absent of palindromes. The permitted pair differences are the coset 1 modulo g; for each permitted d solve (b−1)h=1−d modulo m and choose digits of L with sum a−h(b−1) modulo m. At N=b^h(bL+1)−1 the two digit sums differ by 1−h(b−1) and the first has residue a. This realizes all pairs even for g=m. Negation preserves the coset exactly when g divides two. Counting fixed pairs (m for g=1, none for g=2) proves the three formulas. The classical binary prefix already contains 011 and 110. The frozen finite-prefix verifier was inspected without execution and is not needed for the universal proof.
